name: ALEPH
notes: 'ALEPH: Apparatus for LEP Physics' per the experiment's INSPIRE long_name (src:aleph-inspire-experiment-record).

home.cern's own ALEPH page dates first measured events to 'July 1989', one month ahead of the collaboration-wide August 1989 start used for DELPHI/L3/OPAL; both are recorded (home.cern's July 1989 as the interval start, since it is ALEPH-specific and more precise).

physics_goals.quote: began data-taking in July 1989 and operated for 11 years until the end of LEP programme
physics_goals.value: Make precision measurements of the Z and W bosons produced in electron-positron collisions at LEP

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, used to study the Z and W bosons with great precision, including proving there are exactly three kinds of light neutrino.
summary.technical: General-purpose LEP detector at interaction Point 4: silicon-microstrip vertex detector, inner drift chamber, a 4.4 m long x 3.6 m diameter time projection chamber, electromagnetic and hadron calorimeters and a superconducting coil (6.3 m long x 5.3 m diameter, 1.5 T) providing the magnetic field. Approved by the CERN LEPC on 18 November 1982; took data from July/August 1989 to November 2000.

unique_capabilities.quote: a time projection chamber - 4.4 metres long and 3.6 metres in diameter - to detect charged particles
unique_capabilities.value: A large time-projection chamber (4.4 m long, 3.6 m diameter) inside a 1.5 T superconducting solenoid for precise charged-particle tracking
